problem: Frozen VLMs decompose long-horizon mobile manipulation instructions into plausible skill sequences but propose unavailable skills, lose track of cumulative embodiment state (region, gripper occupancy), and cannot repair plans when execution deviates. Scene-graph and map-based planners need dense geometric models, and querying the VLM every step is slow and token-heavy.
motivation: Skill feasibility in long-horizon MoMa depends on the state left by preceding skills, so errors compound across heterogeneous navigation and manipulation skills. The authors want a map-light, skill-centric interface that captures skill-to-skill dependencies without a dense scene map or VLM training, and that queries the VLM only when needed.
key_idea: Constrain a frozen VLM with a topology-only projection of a Skill-State Graph over a hierarchical skill library, verify cumulative region/gripper state before execution, and trigger graph-grounded repair only when an observed outcome invalidates the remaining plan.
insight: Explicit skill-to-skill dependencies matter more than richer scene descriptions or extra subgoal decomposition: SayPlan* (scene-graph) and DeCo* (subgoal decomposition) stay at 1-35% validity while MoMaStage reaches 96-100%. In the GPT-5.4 nano ablation, topology-only extraction improves initial validity (e.g. 38.3 vs 19.7 for MoMaStage*, RL:Per_Obj) and cuts latency, while verification plus repair lifts final validity to 92.7-100% even from low initial validity. Physical completion remains bounded by low-level skills, since 100% real-world planning validity gives only 60% hard-tier completion.
method: Hierarchical skill library: semantic skills (e.g. left-arm-pick-blue-plate, navigate-from-A-to-B, backed by IL/VLA/RL/rule-based controllers) plus named action skills (open-gripper, retract-arm-to-home, rotate-base) used to bridge states and recover.

Skill-State Graph: directed graph G=(V,E,P,Δ) over semantic skills. The robot state is c=(L,h^l,h^r); each node has a precondition predicate over c and a state variation Δ=(f_L,f^l,f^r) using MOVE/ADD/SUB. Graphs are manually specified.
Topology-only planning: the VLM receives instruction, image and only the task-relevant subgraph G_topo (nodes and adjacency, no P or Δ) and proposes a path of skills.

SSG verifier: replays the candidate from the initial state c_0 taken from proprioception, checking c_{i-1} ⊨ pre(s_i) and applying Δ. On conflict it returns a structured error (step and variable), the VLM repairs, and the plan is re-verified before execution.
Ego-state monitoring: joint encoders, gripper width and tactile signals confirm primitive outcomes without calling the VLM.

Event-driven semantic verification and repair: a VLM scene check against expected Δ runs only when ego signals are inconclusive or the skill changes the scene. On deviation the VLM replans from c_obs over SSG plus action skills, preserving completed subtasks, and each repair is re-verified. Unrepresentable deviations are reported unrecoverable.

setting.backbone: Frozen VLMs: Qwen3.6 Flash (main), Gemini 3.6 Flash, GPT-5.4 nano; low-level skills are pretrained PPO/SAC/BC policies in sim and ACT plus rules on the real robot
setting.training_data: none for the VLM (training-free); underlying skills are pretrained (PPO/SAC/BC in ManiSkill-Hab; ACT on 50 demonstrations per skill on the real robot)
setting.observation: RGB visual observation plus proprioception (joint encoders, gripper width, tactile); named scene regions
setting.action_space: Discrete semantic skill sequences (chosen from SSG nodes) plus named action-skill primitives executed by controllers
setting.privileged: Manually specified SSG, named scene regions and predefined skill library (with preconditions/effects); no dense map or GT scene state stated

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmarks; all results are on the paper's own mshab* tasks and real-robot tiers. Only a representative subset of the 9 simulation configurations and survival steps is listed. Real-world baseline results are given only in a figure.
results: MoMaStage reaches 96.0-100.0% planning validity across all task and skill configurations, versus 1.0-35.3% for VLM-Direct, DeCo* and SayPlan*. It also matches or beats the human-authored open-loop GT sequencing on execution survival at most milestones and has the lowest latency. On the real robot it gets 100% plan validity, 90%/80% completion on easy/medium and 60% on hard, where DeCo* and end-to-end ACT fail.
limitations: SSG, named regions and the skill library are manually specified. The state abstraction covers only region and gripper occupancy, so receptacle state, reachability and grasp feasibility are left to the controllers.
Final task completion is bounded by low-level skill failures. Force-limit exceeded errors dominate in simulation, and the real hard tier drops from 100% validity to 60% completion.

Evaluation is limited to the authors' mshab* setup and one real dual-arm platform, with few baselines (adapted DeCo*, SayPlan*); porting to a new embodiment requires redefining the state tuple, pre and Δ.
